desc:
An ugly number is a positive integer whose only prime factors are 2, 3 and 5 (1 counts as ugly). Listed in increasing order they start

1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, ...

Return the n-th ugly number (1-indexed).

n = 10  -> 12
n = 1   -> 1
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1,690 (the answer then fits in a 32-bit signed integer)
hints: Testing every integer for ugliness is too slow when answers get large. Build the sequence directly instead.
Every ugly number except 1 is a smaller ugly number multiplied by 2, 3 or 5. So the candidates for the next ugly number are the already-found numbers times 2, times 3 and times 5.

Keep a min-heap (with a set to avoid duplicates), or better, three pointers into the sequence built so far: the next value is the smallest of ugly[a]*2, ugly[b]*3, ugly[c]*5, and every pointer that produced it moves forward.
editorial: Heap approach: start with 1. Repeatedly pop the smallest value x, and push 2x, 3x, 5x unless already seen. The n-th pop is the answer. Each pop adds at most three pushes, so the time is O(n log n).

Pointer approach (a merge of three sorted streams): the sequence is the sorted union of {2u}, {3u} and {5u} over all ugly u. Keep three indices a, b, c into the sequence; the next term is min(seq[a]*2, seq[b]*3, seq[c]*5). Advance every index whose product equals that minimum, which also removes duplicates such as 6 = 2*3 = 3*2. This is O(n) time and O(n) space and is the same idea as merging k sorted lists with a heap, just with fixed k = 3.
